results.answer_en: Guardrails are the checks around the model, before and after it. Before: validate input, catch injection, strip personal data, limit scope. After: force the output shape, check claims against the source, block unsupported answers, require a human for actions. We do not trust the model to be right by itself.

results.speaker: short
results.match_question: What is the difference between TF-IDF and embeddings?
results.answer_en: TF-IDF scores words by how often they appear, balanced by how common they are. Embeddings capture meaning, so two sentences with different words can sit close. I used TF-IDF for helpdesk tickets and embeddings for assignment similarity, because students change the words on purpose.

results.answer_en: LangGraph is a state graph: state is the task data, a node is a step, an edge picks the next step including loops. Checkpoints save state. Interrupt pauses for a human, then resumes. I have not used it in production. I would use it for that pause and replay.

results.match_question: Which metric did you use and why?
results.answer_en: Recall on the students who needed support. Most students were fine, so Accuracy looks high even if you miss the ones who matter. Missing a struggling student is worse than one extra follow-up. I still watched Precision so the list did not flood teachers.
